applicability: Checking one scaffold-constrained planar reachable new-contact catch against its matched no-catch crash control
Checking first-observation planning, observed contact phases, support expansion, finite actuation, receipts, and full-horizon retention
claim: In the exact certified BR10.3 Godot/Jolt pair, the active fixture begins with one bearing left distal contact and one unloaded right catch limb, plans on the first post-disturbance observation, creates ordered new TOUCH, LOAD, and BEARING evidence within the declared clock and impact envelope, expands the measured support interval, and returns to the declared stance dwell through the complete horizon using bounded normal-load rate, friction-reserved sagittal commands, finite paired actuators, and complete receipts and contact capacity; the matched no-catch fixture reaches only a late high-speed crash contact and never returns.

evidence.certification_claim_boundary: This campaign can certify only the exact source-pinned BR10.0 deterministic reachable-catch planning scope; BR10.1 observed SEARCH-to-TOUCH-to-LOAD-to-BEARING phase-authority scope; BR10.2 strict sagittal tangent/normal J-transpose force-map scope; and BR10.3 paired active-catch and no-catch-control Godot/Jolt scope. BR10.4 is integrity-only containment and cannot substitute for a milestone program. The BR10.3 analyzer boundary is verbatim: BR10 paired reachable new-contact catch step on the exact inherited BR7 sagittal scaffold: one no-catch control and one active-catch world; one material unpowered out-of-plane guide with in-plane X/Y translation and pitch released; four passive hinges driven only through paired finite joint actuators; one ordinary left distal contact bearing at the declared disturbance while the observed right distal sphere is unloaded and clear; one preparation-only root freeze released exactly with one declared pitch impulse; one deterministic support-expanding plan selected on the first post-disturbance observation; finite swing commands to a world target; observed SEARCH to TOUCH to LOAD to BEARING authority; bounded normal-load rate and friction-reserved sagittal tangent commands mapped through an explicit J-transpose contract; full command-ledger, executor, receipt, and contact-capacity reconciliation; measured support-interval expansion; and a post-catch world-target/posture handoff that retains ordinary contacts through the complete horizon. Commanded contact-force shares are not measured per-foot loads. The positive result establishes only this scaffold-constrained planar reachable catch step and return to the declared stance dwell relative to its matched no-catch crash control. It establishes no per-foot measured load allocation, free-3D standing or bracing, general articulated load-bearing limb, generalized fall arrest, getting up, gait, walking, creature repair, or automatic creature guidance.

program.claim_scope: Fresh active-catch and no-catch-control Godot/Jolt worlds execute complete matched horizons on the exact inherited BR7 sagittal scaffold. At the declared disturbance the left distal contact is bearing and the right limb is unloaded; the planner first acts on the next observation, creates ordered new TOUCH, LOAD, and BEARING evidence within its conservative clock and impact envelope, measurably expands the support interval, and returns to the declared full-horizon stance dwell through finite paired actuators, friction-reserved tangent commands, bounded normal-load rate, complete receipts, and complete contact capacity. The matched no-catch world reaches only a late high-speed crash contact and never returns. No root rescue, foot pin, pose teleport, automatic guidance, free-3D claim, or generalized per-foot measurement is present.

failure_boundaries: The material guide locks out-of-plane translation, roll, and yaw, and the preparation root freeze is part of the fixture
Commanded shares and the local predicted normal-load witness do not establish measured per-foot allocation

mechanism: After the preparation freeze is released with the declared impulse, the active world selects one support-expanding target, drives the unloaded limb through finite paired joint torques, accepts contact only from explicit observations, then uses friction-reserved tangent and bounded normal commands to retain the new ordinary contact and return the scaffolded body to stance. The no-catch world provides the matched crash control.
